title: ICP-Brasil XAdES (AD-RB, AD-RT, AD-RV, AD-RC, AD-RA)
description: XAdES signatures under the ICP-Brasil signature policies (DOC-ICP-15.03: AD-RB, AD-RT, AD-RV, AD-RC and AD-RA) with the icp-brasil trust profile and its signing and validation policies, through the library and the CLI ('simplesign brasil xades sign --icp-policy'). The Sandbox stands in for ICP-Brasil: its trust is added to the profile's (trustProfiles: Sandbox), so its certificates and its TSA play the part of an AC and an ACT; the first section shows that the profile alone trusts only the AC Raiz roots. It complements icp-brasil-pades: only what the policies change in XAdES is here.

sections.title: The ICP-Brasil profile
sections.description: Its anchors are the AC Raiz roots; a certificate that does not chain to them is refused before signing. The Sandbox's trust, added to the profile, lets the rest of the playbook sign with test certificates.

steps.title: Profile alone: a certificate outside ICP-Brasil is refused
steps.description: Only the AC Raiz roots are anchors: the Sandbox's chain is not trusted, and the signer refuses (UntrustedRoot).

sections.title: The policies
sections.description: Each policy writes its identifier and hash (the newest version that accepts the signer's root) and sets the level: AD-RT a signature timestamp from an ACT, AD-RV the complete references, AD-RC the validation values, AD-RA an archive timestamp. The signing certificate is written as XAdES 1.3.2 SigningCertificate, as the XML PAs mandate.

steps.title: AD-RB: the policy identifier
steps.description: The policy's identifier and hash, the newest version that accepts the signer's root; no timestamp (B-B).

steps.title: AD-RT: a signature timestamp from the ACT
steps.description: AD-RB plus a signature timestamp from the ACT (B-T).

steps.title: AD-RV: the complete references to the validation data
steps.description: AD-RT plus the complete references to the certificates and revocation data (the -C extended form).

steps.title: AD-RC: the validation values, protected by a timestamp
steps.description: AD-RV plus the validation values themselves, protected by a timestamp (the -X-L extended form).

steps.title: AD-RA: an archive timestamp
steps.description: AD-RC plus an archive timestamp (the -A extended form).

sections.title: Two phases
sections.description: The server prepares with the public certificate, the key signs elsewhere (an A3 token behind the SimpleSign Agent) and the server completes the policy's level.

steps.title: AD-RT in two phases
steps.description: AD-RT prepared with the public certificate, signed outside, and completed: the timestamp is added in the second phase.

sections.title: Validation
sections.description: The icp-brasil validation policy checks the policy each signature declares: its hash, its period and, from AD-RT, the timestamp.

steps.title: AD-RB validates under the icp-brasil profile
steps.description: Validates the AD-RB file with the ICP-Brasil profile and policy.

steps.title: AD-RT validates under the icp-brasil profile
steps.description: Validates the AD-RT file, its signature time-stamp included.
